study_identification_part.si4_title: Effects of anterior temporal lobe resection on cortical morphology

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Quantify how anterior temporal lobe resection (ATLR) affects cortical morphology using traditional measures (thickness, total and exposed surface area) and independent measures (K, I, S), accounting for age/sex/scanner effects via a normative model.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Scanning protocol modeled as random effect in GAMM normative model; site-specific controls (91 from NHNN/Chalfont matching patients' protocols) used to inform protocol-specific effects; large NKI dataset used for robust age range coverage despite protocol mismatch; separate processing of controls with/without temporal lobes to match ipsilateral/contralateral patient data
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: We trained a model with the formula ... where b is a model coefficient, s is a smooth spline, ε is the error term, and y is one of the measures p T, p A't, or p A'e, using restricted maximum likelihood as the method for smoothing parameter estimation. We used the controls to provide a normative model of age and sex with scanning protocol as a random effect. Even though the large NKI data set did not match the patients in scanning protocol, we used them for training to ensure we had robust models for the entire age range, given that the site-specific control data sets were relatively small (Rutherford et al., 2023). The site-specific controls matching the patients then informed effects for the specific scanning protocols.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ATLR induces widespread cortical morphology changes ipsilaterally (orbitofrontal/inferior frontal, pre/postcentral, supramarginal, lingual, lateral occipital) and contralaterally (lateral occipital, inferior frontal/frontal pole), with complementary patterns across traditional and independent measures (K, I, S).
